messages.content: 請顯示2019年從舊金山被定罪的所有洗錢罪犯，以及2018年從德克薩斯州被定罪的洗錢罪犯。

function.name: law_crimes_search
function.description: Locate individuals based on their crime conviction and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City or state where the crime was committed.

year.description: The year when the crime was committed.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to display all money laundering criminals convicted from San Francisco (city) in 2019, and those from Texas (state) in 2018.

We have a tool "law_crimes_search" with arguments: crime type, location, year. We can call it twice:

1st call: crime="money laundering", location="San Francisco", year=2019
2nd call: crime="money laundering", location="Texas", year=2018

But we need to consider if location expects city or state? It says "City or state". So it's fine.

We'll produce calls accordingly. Then after receiving results, we'll format them as requested. We'll use Chinese formatting. Probably list each convict's name, age, gender, etc. But we don't know what data returned will contain; but likely includes id, name, age, gender, address, phone, email, criminal record ID, case details, court info, sentencing info, etc. We'll just output whatever fields exist.

Thus first step: call tool for SF 2019. Then second call for TX 2018. After both responses, combine into one response. Use Chinese text. Let's do that.
